subject: Evidence request — DPIA sampling, Art.28/30 artifacts & KMS rotation logs
messages:
From: Martin Hsu <mhsu@novamedical.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: audit-team@novamedical.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: DPIA follow-up — sampling of logs + KMS proof for pilot

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move our pilot into security review, the audit team has a couple of targeted asks to close our DPIA and Art.28/30 checklist before the scoped proof-of-concept begins. Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide the following artifacts for a sampling exercise (we only need representative extracts, not full dumps):

1) Processing ledger excerpt (Art.30): CSV with a 7-day sample that includes: processing purpose, categories of data processed, encoder model id, and originating tenant id (pseudonymized if necessary).
2) Access/audit logs for the same 7-day window showing service account and operator actions related to loading keys and model version rollouts.
3) KMS rotation proof: signed report that shows per-tenant key rotation events + key IDs for the past 90 days.
4) Subprocessor attestations: current inventory as of today and whether any planned rotations are scheduled.

We understand you may need to redact or pseudonymize fields; we just need enough to validate data flows and retention settings for the DPIA. Please indicate expected turnaround for a packaged evidence set and any legal intake (DPA amendment / NDA) you need prior to sharing.

Best,
Martin
Martin Hsu
Sr. InfoSec Manager — Nova Medical

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Martin Hsu <mhsu@novamedical.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPIA follow-up — DPIA sampling, Art.28/30 artifacts & KMS rotation logs

Hi Martin —

Thanks for the clear list. We can provide a scoped evidence pack that meets those asks. High level plan and constraints:

- What we'll provide: a redacted processing_ledger_excerpt.csv (sample window you specified), filtered access/audit logs with operator and service-account events, and a KMS rotation summary that includes key IDs and rotation timestamps (we will not share private key material).
- Subprocessors: we'll include the current inventory and the onboarding date + TELOS for each (we'll flag any near-term changes).
- Timing: we can assemble a first pack within 6 business days from confirmation of the minimal legal scope. If you need it earlier, we can compress to 3 business days but will limit sampling to 72 hours.
- Legal: if you need us to attach a DPA amendment or a short evidence-sharing addendum, please send the drafting checklist; otherwise we will proceed under the existing DPA and our standard evidence-sharing procedure.

Next steps: can you confirm (A) the redaction level allowed for tenant identifiers (pseudonymized vs. hashed id), and (B) whether your audit team requires a notarized KMS rotation report or an internal-signed TXT dump will suffice?

I'll coordinate with Karthik and Grace to produce the artifacts and will share a Drive folder once we have a green light.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 10:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPIA follow-up — DPIA sampling, Art.28/30 artifacts & KMS rotation logs

Martin / team —

Technical clarifications from the runtime side so the sample is useful for your DPIA:

- Processing ledger excerpt: we can export Art.30 ledger rows with pseudonymized tenant_id (sha256) and enumerated processing purpose tags. We'll include model_id and quantization profile columns. Note: KV cache activity is per-request and not persisted in the ledger; we can instead provide prefix-cache hit/miss aggregate counts for the sample window.

- Access logs: we will provide VCS deployment events, operator console sessions (start/end), and service-account key usage events for the window. We will exclude ephemeral debug tokens and will redact session.cookie values.

- KMS rotation: Redwood supports per-tenant envelope keys stored in the customer's KMS or our managed KMS depending on deployment. For hosted accounts we can provide a rotation report showing envelope key ID, rotation timestamp, and signer fingerprint. For on-prem/private KMS customers we only provide metadata (no key material).

- Sampling method: propose stratified sampling across three workload buckets (low/medium/high latency) and include at least 50 ledger rows per bucket. If Nova wants a different stratification, tell us which tenants to prioritize.

I will produce a short README that explains the columns and our redaction rules. Expect the initial folder link from me once Lauren confirms the redaction level and legal scope.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Platform Security & Privacy | Redwood Inference
[attachment: processing_ledger_excerpt.csv (csv)]
From: Martin Hsu <mhsu@novamedical.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: audit-team@novamedical.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPIA follow-up — DPIA sampling, Art.28/30 artifacts & KMS rotation logs

Lauren, Karthik —

This looks good. A couple of follow-ups before you package: 

- Redaction level: hashed tenant ids (sha256) are fine, but we need a mapping exercise if we escalate — include a separate mapping protocol doc on how to re-identify under a legal order (even if we don't receive the mapping now).
- KMS: we require a signed rotation report (internal-signed is acceptable) that includes the rotation window and key IDs. We do not need private key material.
- Sampling acceptance criteria: the audit team wants the stratified sampling you suggested, and the 50-row minimum per bucket is acceptable.

Can you also confirm whether the samples will include any customer PII fields (we'd prefer zero PII in the ledger export)? If there's any residual identifiers (email hashes, etc.), please detail the hash algorithm and any salts used.

If you can get an initial pack to us by EOD next Friday (28 May), that would keep our internal review on track.

Thanks —
Martin
